sentences.text: Net interest income compounded at 8.4% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, while noninterest income compounded at 6.2% [F111][F112].
Net income compounded at 9.7% and diluted EPS at 13.9% over the same window, so per-share growth outpaced earnings growth [F113][F115].
Net interest income fell to $52.3 billion in FY2021, then rose 27.5% in FY2022 and 33.8% in FY2023 [F6][D149][D174].
The cited passages explain this only for the Corporate segment, where net revenue rose to $8.0 billion on higher net interest income due to higher rates [P36].
Net income fell 20.0% in FY2020 and rose 65.8% in FY2021, as the provision swung from $17.5 billion to a $9.3 billion release [D94][D118][X142][X143].
Commercial And Investment Bank noninterest income reached $53.8 billion in FY2025, up from $48.3 billion in FY2024 [S134][S133].
Noninterest revenue rose 2.4% to $87.0 billion in FY2025 on higher Markets revenue, largely offset by the absence of the $7.9 billion Visa share gain recorded in 2024 [D222][F20][P27].
Net interest income grew 3.1% to $95.4 billion, driven by Markets net interest income and Card Services revolving balances, largely offset by deposit margin compression [D221][F10][P28].
Asia-Pacific and EMEA each added 1.2pp to FY2025 revenue growth, against 0.2pp from North America [D301][D276][D251].
Noninterest expense grew 4.2% in FY2025 against revenue growth of 2.8%, so costs outran revenue [D225][D226].
The FY2025 efficiency ratio of 52.4% sits near the window low of 51.7% and well below the window median of 57.2% [D207][D331][D333].
That ratio is below the banks peer median of 61.7%, the lowest among the seven peers [D207][D337][D336].
Noninterest expense reached $95.6 billion, driven by higher compensation, including revenue-related pay and headcount growth [X137][P26].
The credit-loss provision rose to 7.8% of revenue from 6.0%, including a $2.2 billion allowance addition tied to the Apple Card transaction [D208][D185][P18].
Rising provisions and costs explain why net income fell 2.6% despite higher revenue [D214][D226].
Operating cash flow is not a meaningful earnings-quality measure for a bank, and was an outflow of $147.8 billion in FY2025 [F60].
Cash used in operations reflected higher trading assets, securities borrowed and loans held-for-sale, which are balance-sheet activity rather than weaker earnings [F60][P21].
Capital return is the better test: buybacks plus dividends were $48.2 billion in FY2025 against net income of $57.0 billion [D205][F30].
Shareholders' equity rose 5.1% to $362 billion in FY2025, while loans reached 57.3% of deposits from 55.0% [D220][F110][D211][D188].
Cash and equivalents fell to $343 billion from $469 billion, driven by Markets activities, higher securities and higher loans [F100][F99][P24].
Return on average equity of 16.1% ranks at the 100th percentile of seven banks peers, against a peer median of 11.8% [D213][D338][D339].
Buybacks rose to $31.6 billion from $18.8 billion, and the diluted share count fell 3.4% [X102][X101][D224].
Credit costs are rising: the provision reached 7.8% of revenue in FY2025, the highest since FY2020's 14.6% and the 75th percentile of four peers [D208][D88][D340].
The peer median is 6.0%, so JPMorgan provisions more than most of the group [D341].
Criticized wholesale exposure rose to $48.5 billion from $44.7 billion, primarily on downgrades and new lending commitments [P2].
Nonperforming exposure rose $478 million, driven by downgrades in Technology, Media & Telecommunications, Oil & Gas and Utilities [P3].
Data quality: FY2021 to FY2025 net income in the table comes from the proxy and is rounded, for example $57,000 million against the 10-K's $57,048 million in FY2025 [R1][F30][X20].
An efficiency ratio above the FY2025 level of 52.4% would confirm cost growth outrunning revenue, while a return toward the 51.7% window low would reverse it, in the FY2026 10-K [D207][D331].
A provision above 7.8% of revenue would confirm worsening credit costs, while a fall toward the 6.0% peer median would reverse it, in the FY2026 10-K [D208][D341].
Net interest income excluding Markets below the FY2025 level of $92.6 billion, which was flat on the prior year, would confirm deposit margin compression, in the FY2026 10-K [P28].
